subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` keep the per-scope `/workspace` writable while still hiding the agent workspace, or should `none` remain a read-only sandbox workspace?
rationale: The source fix is clear, but this choice changes sandbox write authorization and current docs/tests reflect both security and usability interpretations.

options.title: Approve isolated writable `none`
options.body: Treat only `ro` as the read-only mode, keep the agent workspace hidden in `none`, and repair the mount/bridge/tool/docs surfaces together.

options.title: Keep `none` read-only
options.body: Preserve the current stricter behavior and update docs/tool exposure so `none` no longer implies writable sandbox work.

options.title: Add explicit opt-in mode
options.body: Keep current `none` semantics and introduce a separate approved mode only if maintainers want another sandbox write policy.

recommendation.title: Approve isolated writable `none`
recommendation.body: Treat only `ro` as the read-only mode, keep the agent workspace hidden in `none`, and repair the mount/bridge/tool/docs surfaces together.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently worked on adjacent sandbox write-tool gating and are a plausible owner for coordinating the security/product boundary.
